evals.name: run-rancher-2-12-air
evals.prompt: We run Rancher 2.12 on an air-gapped RKE2 cluster with the bundled Logging app (rancher-logging 107.0.2+up4.10.0-rancher.15) in cattle-logging-system. We're tired of it being stuck on an ancient operator. Plan a migration to the upstream logging-operator that keeps our existing Flows/ClusterOutputs and the fluentd disk buffers, with minimal logging downtime. We mirror images through Harbor.
evals.expected_output: Leads with the release-secret strategy: scale down operator, delete sh.helm.release.v1.rancher-logging{,-crd} secrets (NOT helm uninstall rancher-logging-crd, which cascade-deletes all CRs + data plane - no resource-policy keep). Air-gap prep FIRST (6.7.0 image list into Harbor, OCI chart mirror). CRDs via kubectl apply --server-side --force-conflicts (client-side fails, huge CRDs). Preserve buffer PVCs by keeping Logging name rancher-logging-root + controlNamespace. Pruning pre-flight for removed fields (sumologic/enhanceK8s/enabledNamespaces/nodeAgents - silent, not errors). Target 6.7.0 (CVE + 6.6.0 regression) and surfaces the CVE-2026-54680 urgency as a migration motivation. Mentions journald aggregator DaemonSet delta and rollback via backed-up release secrets (stuck-finalizer handling on CR deletion is a bonus).
assertions: The plan preserves the existing Flows/ClusterOutputs by deleting the Helm release secrets (sh.helm.release.v1.rancher-logging* / rancher-logging-crd*) rather than running an uninstall of the chart's CRD release
The plan explicitly warns that uninstalling the rancher-logging-crd release would cascade-delete the custom resources and the running fluentd/fluent-bit data plane
The plan applies the new CRDs with server-side apply and conflict forcing (e.g. kubectl apply --server-side --force-conflicts) rather than a plain client-side apply
The plan keeps the fluentd buffer PVCs by reusing the existing Logging resource name (rancher-logging-root) and the cattle-logging-system controlNamespace, and does not delete that namespace
The plan performs air-gap mirroring of the target operator images and chart into Harbor before any cluster-side change begins

The plan includes a pre-flight check for CR fields that the newer operator silently drops (e.g. sumologic, enhanceK8s, ClusterOutput enabledNamespaces, nodeAgents) and states that these are pruned without error rather than rejected
The target upstream operator version is 6.7.0 or newer, with a stated reason for not stopping at 6.6.0
The plan provides a rollback path that restores the backed-up Helm release secrets and the original operator

evals.name: security-team-asking-whether-rancher
evals.prompt: Security team is asking whether our Rancher 2.13 clusters are exposed through the logging stack. We have rancher-logging 108.0.2+up4.10.0-rancher.18 deployed, project owners manage their own log Flows. What's the actual exposure and what do we tell them?
evals.expected_output: Names CVE-2026-54680 (GHSA-mjqf-28ph-426h, CVSS 9.9): operator 4.10.0 is in the affected range (<=6.5.2), config injection via newline in Flow/Output/secret values -> RCE in aggregator. Trigger tier: project-owners CAN trigger (logging-admin ClusterRole aggregated to admin, verbs * on flows/outputs) - directly relevant since they author Flows. No SUSE fix exists; fix requires upstream 6.6.0+/6.7.0 (migration). Blast radius: output credentials + SA cloud roles. fluent-bit 3.1.8 CVEs framed precisely as version-in-range but not exploitable in default pipeline. Offers interim mitigations (RBAC audit, alert on CR mutations) while recommending the exit.
assertions: The answer identifies CVE-2026-54680 (GHSA-mjqf-28ph-426h, CVSS 9.9) and states that the deployed operator 4.10.0 falls inside the affected range (<= 6.5.2)

The answer describes the vulnerability mechanism as unescaped rendering of CR/secret values into the fluentd config, where a newline in a Flow/Output field injects arbitrary fluentd directives leading to code execution in the aggregator
The answer concludes that project owners can trigger the vulnerability because the chart's logging-admin ClusterRole is aggregated into the built-in admin role with full verbs on flows/outputs
The answer states that no vendor/SUSE patch is available and that remediation requires moving to the upstream 6.x line (6.6.0+/6.7.0), not a Rancher chart update or Rancher version upgrade
The answer describes the blast radius as compromise of the log output credentials held by the aggregator plus any cloud identity attached to its service account
The answer characterizes fluent-bit 3.1.8 as version-in-range for known CVEs but not exploitable in the default collection pipeline, rather than as an active RCE
The answer offers interim mitigations that can be applied before the migration completes (such as restricting who can create/modify Flows and Outputs, or alerting on CR changes)

evals.name: found-old-rke2-cluster-where
evals.prompt: Found an old RKE2 cluster where someone removed the Rancher logging app years ago but there are still logging.banzaicloud.io CRDs from 2022, a rancher-logging-crd helm release, and a handful of ClusterOutputs sitting there inactive. We now want a fresh upstream logging-operator install on it. Anything to watch out for before I just helm install?
evals.expected_output: Identifies the stale-debris state and THE trap: naive helm install silently skips the existing old CRDs (crds/ dir semantics) -> mixed old/new CRD generations with no error (3.17-era ships only 7 of 16 CRDs). Path: salvage/back up the orphaned ClusterOutputs first (still-valid destination config), then either helm uninstall rancher-logging-crd (safe here - nothing running, cascade harmless) for a clean slate, or server-side-apply 6.7.0 CRDs over + delete the orphaned helm release secret. Also checks/cleans legacy clusterloggings/projectloggings.management.cattle.io CRDs. Recommends re-authoring salvaged config as 6.7-era CRs rather than verbatim re-apply.
assertions: The answer identifies that a plain helm install will not replace the pre-existing 2022 CRDs because the chart's bundled CRDs are skipped when those CRDs already exist, leaving the new operator running against stale schemas with no error emitted
The answer notes that the old CRD set is incomplete relative to the current one, so some required custom resource kinds would be missing entirely
The answer instructs backing up or exporting the orphaned ClusterOutputs before any CRD deletion or replacement

The answer states that deleting the old CRDs / uninstalling the rancher-logging-crd release is acceptable in this specific situation because no operator or data plane is running, while making clear the CRs would be removed with them
The answer offers server-side apply of the current CRDs plus removal of the orphaned rancher-logging-crd Helm release secret as an alternative to deleting the CRDs
The answer tells the reader to also check for and clean up legacy management.cattle.io logging CRDs (clusterloggings/projectloggings)
The answer recommends re-authoring the salvaged ClusterOutputs against the current API schema instead of re-applying the 2022 manifests verbatim
